page: Microsoft Azure D1ps_v7 is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture. Virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is provisioned with a single dedicated ARM virtual processor and 4.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external persistent block storage such as Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not present, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not bundled with the deployment. The single-core arm64 environment relies on a 64-bit ARM instruction set without x86-specific vector or matrix extensions like AVX or AMX.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D1ps_v7 offers an economical footprint for lightweight architectures by leveraging the power-efficient characteristics of ARM hardware alongside dedicated core execution. The configuration is suited for low-traffic web services, background utilities, development and test nodes, microservices, and small containerized workloads that do not require high computational parallelism or local scratch disks.
description: Microsoft Azure D1ps_v7 is a general purpose virtual machine powered by 64-bit ARM architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 1 dedicated arm64 vCPU paired with 4.0 GB of RAM, conforming to a balanced 1:4 processor-to-memory profile. It includes no local storage, requiring network-attached options such as Premium Storage for persistent file handling, and operates without GPU hardware acceleration. The architecture provides consistent single-threaded processing using dedicated CPU allocation while maintaining low power consumption and cost overhead typical of ARM-based hardware. Because of its single-core configuration and modest memory footprint, the instance is best suited for small web services, low-overhead containerized tasks, development sandboxes, and foundational microservices.
